# aeneid-011 review (Aeneid II.195–286), two passes

Findings: **major 7, medium 10, low 12** (29 changed) plus 8 refused/left. All edits made by script; `t` untouched, `l` line counts preserved (checked).

## Changes
Major
1. u8 (212) n: 'visu' called "the supine"; it is the ablative of the noun 'visus' (cause). Fixed.
2. u17 (232) n: Sinon's 'effigies' cited as line 183; it is 'effigiem' at 184. Fixed.
3. u38 (278) n: 'circum' "after its noun (anastrophe)"; it precedes 'muros', separated by 'plurima'. Fixed; also dropped the odd "indicative because narrator's fact" sentence.
4. u36 (273) n: 'traiectus lora' glossed "pierced through as to the thongs" (wrong; the thongs are what was passed through). Fixed.
5. u18 (234) n: "Aeneas, who has been telling the story as an observer, now says 'we'" is false (he says 'we' from 212 and 195). Fixed.
6. u36 n: Patroclus "still bearing the marks of his death" (not in Iliad 23). Removed.
7. u32 i: 'demissum lapsi per funem' (plural, all the captains) attached to Ulysses alone. Moved to the whole company.

Medium
8. u13 n and u37 n: "retained accusative" used for 'vittas' (accusative of respect) and 'exuvias indutus'; relabelled.
9. u12 i: "twice clasped about his waist" read as passive; now "having twice clasped him about the waist"; note adds that 'terga' is the accusative kept after 'dati'.
10. u14 n: "the bull of line 202" (not in the text) replaced by "echoes his own sacrifice"; Iliad 20.403–405 reduced to "Iliad (book 20)" (see refused/unverified). u14 i: "glancing axe" to "ill-aimed axe" (agrees with l).
11. u15 i: "goddess of Triton" (misleading) to "Tritonian goddess"; n: "horse replaces the image" to "offered in Sinon's tale".
12. u19 l: "They gird all" read 'omnes' as object; now "All gird themselves".
13. u36 l: "run through ... swollen" garbled; now "through the feet, swollen, pierced with thongs".
14. u32 n: 'Pelides' "patronymic of Achilles, here his son" corrected (from Peleus; Neoptolemus is the grandson); "principal figure in the next part" softened.
15. u29 n: invented "enough light to steer, not to be seen" removed; "island of the first part" made a real reference.
16. u3 i: echo "my flesh creeps at the telling" rephrased: "the very telling of it makes me shudder".
17. u29 i: echo "friendly silence of the quiet moon" rephrased: "in the kindly hush of the silent moon".

Low
18. About: "his lies" (ambiguous) to "Sinon's lies"; "at the shore" (not in text) to "at the altars"; "do not see it" to "do not heed it".
19. u0 n: "triple" non/neque list is fourfold.
20. u1 n: "all through the book" to "often".
21. u2 n: "the stated rites" clarified; "at the shore" claim softened.
22. u3 n: 'gemini… angues' separation described accurately.
23. u5 n: 'terga' plural explained (two snakes).
24. u7 n: added accusative of respect for 'oculos' (the construction is first met here, before 'vittas').
25. u11 n: 'auxilio' dative of purpose softened ("most naturally").
26. u17 n: added that 233 is a half-line; 'simulacrum'/'numina' named as accusative subjects; 'numina' "common" softened.
27. u21 n, u25 n (dative 'fatis' reworded), u26 n ("joke" to bitter irony; subjunctive described as hindsight, not "reason"), u31 n ('patefactus' "having been opened"), u33 i/n ("buried in sleep and wine" varied; "revels" invented), u34 i ("thrown open" vs 'patentibus'), u36 i (opening reworded), u39 n ('virum'), u42 n (genitives), u44 i ("And why" to "Or why", for 'aut').
28–29. u33 and u36 small wording items in the lines above.

## Refused / left
- Iliad cites at 223–224 and Hector/Patroclus: network blocked (scaife.perseus.org), so no public-domain text could be checked. Kept only at book level (Iliad 20 bull simile; Iliad 22 dragging; Iliad 23 Patroclus; Iliad 17 spoils; Iliad 15–16 fire), which I am confident of; line numbers dropped.
- Gerundive indirect statement 232–233: verified as correct (accusative + gerundive with 'esse' understood after 'conclamant'); kept, clarified.
- u26 l "We, the shrines of the gods, wretched": reads oddly but is word-order transparent; left.
- u23 "quater… an ill omen", u13 'tendit' + infinitive, u37 'redit' as historic present (metre requires short -dit, so present): left, true.
- 2.197 "Larisaeus Achilles": scanner leaves -us unelided (correct: -s never elides), valid hexameter; left.
- 2.199 'maius' (ius long), 2.264 (et- long, Epeos by synizesis, cost 1.8), 2.260 (equus quus long): scanner fits are valid hexameters but rest on licences I could not confirm from a public-domain prosody reference; left, not added.
- No hiatus lines in this part (-s and consonant endings never elide; elisions all handled).
